t: What Automated Organ Preservation Systems Is
title: What Automated Organ Preservation Systems Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Automated preservation keeps donor organs alive longer: normothermic perfusion machines oxygenating and repairing organs outside the body — expanding the donor pool and improving transplants. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Automated Organ Preservation Systems: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Automated Organ Preservation Systems in one line: Automated preservation keeps donor organs alive longer: normothermic perfusion machines oxygenating and repairing organs outside the body — expanding the donor pool and improving transplants.
Why it matters: More viable organs means shorter waitlists and better outcomes..
Where it is used: heart, lung, liver, kidney transplant..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of Automated Organ Preservation Systems
title: Current Research State of Automated Organ Preservation Systems
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Normothermic perfusion became standard for lungs/livers; hearts transplanted after machine perfusion; organ repair on-pump demonstrated. Research focuses on repair and assessment. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Automated Organ Preservation Systems currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.

Leading approaches: normothermic perfusion, hypothermic oxygenated, repair.
Key institutions and programs: transplant device firms.
What would change the timeline: the challenges record lists the blockers.
